- G (zone-centre E2g) near 1580 cm-1 and 2D (second order of zone-boundary TO phonons) near 2700 cm-1 at

  sits 3 to 5 cm-1 above bulk graphite (Ferrari et al. 2006, PRL 97, 187401; arXiv cond-mat/0606284, p.2).
  [consensus]
- D' near 1620 cm-1, D+D', 2D' and D+D'' are further double-resonance bands; 2D is present without defects
  (Ferrari and Basko 2013, Nat. Nanotechnol. 8, 235; arXiv 1306.5856, Fig. 1g, pp.3-6).
- Peak areas are more robust than heights: perturbations that only change phonon lifetimes conserve area
  (Ferrari and Basko 2013, p.14). State whether a ratio is I (height) or A (area).

## Thickness and stacking
- 2L Bernal: 2D broader, upshifted, four components; up to 5 layers the 2D shape still changes; above 5
  layers hardly distinguishable from graphite (Ferrari 2006, p.2, Fig. 2b,c). [consensus]
- A single-Lorentzian 2D is not proof of 1L: turbostratic graphite also has one 2D peak, about twice as wide
  and upshifted about 20 cm-1, often with a D peak (Ferrari and Basko 2013, p.9). Grown (CVD) films need this
  check. [consensus]
- Twisted bilayer (Kim et al. 2012, PRL 108, 246103; arXiv 1201.4221, pp.4-6, Figs. 2-3; 633 nm): below about
  8 deg strong-coupling spectra; above about 13 deg close to 1L. G intensity rises more than thirty-fold near
  10 to 11 deg at 633 nm; the resonance angle grows with laser energy (about 13 deg at 514 nm). 2D blueshift vs
  1L is non-monotonic (up to 22 cm-1 at 10 deg). Below 10 deg the 2D area is about half that of two decoupled
  layers.
- Twist also activates non-dispersive superlattice peaks (one in 1350 to 1550 cm-1, one near 1620 cm-1;
  Ferrari and Basko 2013, p.9) named R and R' in later work. A huge G with weak 2D at one laser line means
  "check twist resonance", not "thick flake".
- Bernal (ABA) vs rhombohedral (ABC) trilayer: distinct 2D line shapes; ABA has a higher intensity-weighted mean
  2D shift than ABC with similar dispersion (Lui et al. 2011, Nano Lett. 11, 164; arXiv 1011.3021, SI p.9).
  Thicker stacks have intermediate stackings; far-field imaging can miss sub-micron domains (Lu et al. 2025,
  Nature 637; doi 10.1038/s41586-024-08470-1, p.7, via Lit-RAG).
- Shear (C) mode near 31 cm-1 in 2L scales with N but lies below many notch/edge filters; absence of C is not
  evidence of 1L (Ferrari and Basko 2013, p.2). LO+ZO' combination near 1700 to 1750 cm-1 also tracks N.

- Uniaxial strain splits G into G+ and G- (-10.8 and -31.7 cm-1/%), 2D -64 cm-1/% (Mohiuddin 2009 via Ferrari
  and Basko 2013, p.20, Eq. S10). Biaxial strain shifts without splitting (same, p.20). [consensus]
- G stiffens and narrows for both electron and hole doping (non-adiabatic Kohn anomaly); 2D rises for holes and
  softens only at high electron doping; I(2D)/I(G) falls strongly with doping (Das et al. 2008, Nat.
  Nanotechnol. 3, 210; arXiv 0709.1174, abstract and pp.4-5). [consensus]
- Separate strain and doping by the (Pos G, Pos 2D) vector plot: strain line slope 2.2 +- 0.2 (Lee et al. 2012,
  Nat. Commun. 3, 1024; arXiv 1209.0234, p.3, Fig. 2). Model assumptions (514.5 nm origin, hole doping) limit
  transfer to other lasers or electron doping. [disputed in detail, widely used]

  pp.18-19, Fig. S3). Annealing on SiO2 raises G and 2D by about 25 cm-1 (hole doping) (Lee 2012, p.3).

  so one ratio gives two densities; FWHM(G) decides: about 14 cm-1 through stage 1, much larger in stage 2

- Defect type from I(D)/I(D') in stage 1: about 13 sp3, about 7 vacancy, about 3.5 boundaries (Eckmann et al.
  2012, Nano Lett. 12, 3925; arXiv 1207.2058, abstract, p.6). Only valid in stage 1. [one group, often reproduced]

  than 2x in their example (Bruna et al. 2014, ACS Nano; arXiv 1405.4264, p.5). Check doping before L_D.
- Raman-silent defects: perfect zigzag edges, charged impurities, intercalants, strain give no D peak (Ferrari
  and Basko 2013, p.11). No D peak does not mean defect-free in every sense.
- Edges: D only from armchair-like segments; I(D) proportional to cos^2 theta (cos^4 with parallel analyzer)
  to the edge; I(D)min/I(D)max measures edge disorder (Ferrari and Basko 2013, p.8). A D peak confined to
  edges in a map is an edge effect, not bulk damage.

  SiO2 (Neumann et al. 2015, Nat. Commun. 6, 8429; arXiv 1406.7771, p.2, Fig. 1h). FWHM(2D) is a flatness and
  quality metric.

- Supported 1L: G -0.016, 2D -0.034 cm-1/K, 83 to 373 K (Calizo et al. 2007; arXiv 0708.1223, Table I p.7).
  Suspended 1L: 2D -0.072, G -0.044 cm-1/K (Chen et al., relayed by Lee et al. 2011, PRB 83, 081419; arXiv
  1103.3337, p.2). The difference is substrate thermal-expansion strain: coefficients do not transfer
  between supported and suspended samples. [consensus on the cause]
- Stokes/anti-Stokes thermometry is biased in graphene because incident and scattered resonance windows differ
  (Ferrari and Basko 2013, p.12).

  cm-1/eV in stage 2 (Cancado 2011, p.5; Ferrari and Basko 2013, p.7). Never compare D or 2D positions across
  lasers. I(D)/I(G) scales with lambda^4 (Cancado 2011).
- Twist resonances and doping-blocked 2D are laser-energy specific (Kim 2012; Ferrari and Basko 2013 Fig. S3).

  so use a second wavelength (Purdie et al. 2018, Nat. Commun. 9, 5387; doi 10.1038/s41467-018-07558-3, p.6,

- 2D at about 2700 cm-1 is outside many short-range acquisitions; a "missing 2D" may be range, not physics.

- G position alone cannot separate strain and doping; use the G-2D vector and FWHM(G).

- Exfoliated or CVD or epitaxial; transfer and anneal history; gate or electrolyte; height or area ratios.
- Spectral resolution and calibration reference; mapped area and number of spectra.

input.summary: The defect density rises monotonically with dose. Doses 1–3 are in the low-defect "stage 1" regime, where the D/G height ratio rises 0.25 → 0.57 → 1.19. With the Cancado 2011 relation at 532 nm this gives an inter-defect distance L_D of about 24 → 16 → 11 nm, i.e. n_D of about 5.6e10 → 1.3e11 → 2.7e11 cm^-2 (±~14 % from the relation's constant, plus the ratio uncertainty). Dose 3 is already at the edge of the relation's validity (L_D ≥ 10 nm). Dose 4 has crossed into stage 2. D and G are both strongly broadened (D about 41–61 cm^-1, G+D' about 36–47 cm^-1, depending on the baseline model), D' is merged into G, and the 2D band is nearly gone (<2 % of its dose 1 height). I_D/I_G has dropped back to 0.57, so the L_D relation does not apply. I estimate L_D ≲ 3 nm (n_D ≳ 3.5e12 cm^-2) from the stage boundary only. Given I_D/I_D' ≈ 6–7 in stage 1, the damage looks vacancy-like, but that rests on a weak D' band.

observations.finding: The D band grows strongly and steadily over doses 1–3 while G stays about constant, so the I(D)/I(G) ratio rises. G stays narrow (about 14 cm^-1), which places these spectra in stage 1 (point-defect regime).
observations.evidence: Three-Lorentzian fit of D, G and D' on a linear baseline, 1200–1750 cm^-1. D height 700 → 2047 → 2970 counts; G height 2808 → 3597 → 2494. I_D/I_G (heights) 0.249 → 0.569 → 1.191; by areas 0.26 → 0.60 → 1.26. D position 1345.9 → 1347.3 → 1346.8 cm^-1, FWHM 14.5 / 14.7 / 14.6 cm^-1. G position 1580.3 / 1580.6 / 1580.4 cm^-1, FWHM 13.9 / 14.0 / 13.8 cm^-1. The rl_series fit agrees (D height/G height 0.092/0.366 etc. after its own baseline; D FWHM about 14, G about 12–13). Si offset +0.18 to +0.21 cm^-1 in all spectra, so there is no calibration drift.

observations.finding: The point-defect relation gives L_D and n_D for doses 1–3. Roughly 2× more defects at dose 2 and roughly 5× more at dose 3, relative to dose 1.
observations.evidence: apply_relation graphene_defect_distance_from_ID_IG, laser 532 nm, using height ratios. Dose 1: L_D 24.1 ± 3.3 nm, n_D 5.6e10 cm^-2. Dose 2: 15.9 ± 2.2 nm, 1.28e11 cm^-2. observations.finding: Dose 4 is in stage 2 (high-defect branch). The D and G bands are strongly broadened, D' is no longer resolved from G, and the 2D band has almost vanished. The L_D relation is therefore not valid, and L_D is only bounded.
observations.evidence: Two-peak fit gives D at 1352.2 cm^-1 with FWHM 61 cm^-1 (the rl_series fit, with a different baseline, gives 1351.9 cm^-1 and 41 cm^-1). observations.evidence: I_D/I_D' = 6.0 (dose 1), 6.2 (dose 2), 6.9 (dose 3), with D' at about 1620–1621 cm^-1 and FWHM 11–13 cm^-1. The D' height is only 116 / 331 / 432 counts against noise of about 60 counts, and the uncertainty on dose 1 is large (D' FWHM ± 4 cm^-1).

caveats: The I_D/I_G ratio is non-monotonic in defect density: it peaks near L_D of about 3 nm and then falls. A single ratio therefore maps to two L_D values. The G FWHM and the 2D band tell the two branches apart. Dose 4 has a lower I_D/I_G than dose 3 but is the most damaged, so ratio alone would mislead.

The Cancado constant was calibrated with Ar+ ion bombardment at 514.5, 632.8 and 785 nm. The tool allows 400–786 nm, so 532 nm is inside its validity range, but this is an interpolation. The lambda^4 scaling and the ±0.5 on 1.8e-9 give about ±14 % on L_D. Absolute numbers carry a larger systematic error than the quoted ±.
Dose 3 (L_D = 11 nm) sits at the lower validity limit (≥ 10 nm) and its I_D/I_G is above 1. The relation probably begins to deviate from linear there, so n_D at dose 3 may be somewhat off.

The relation assumes point defects and low doping. Doping lowers D and D' at a fixed defect count, so ignoring E_F about 0.5 eV could underestimate n_D by more than 2×. Edge or boundary contributions to D (the laser spot may include an edge) would be mistaken for point defects. A single spot per dose cannot separate these.
Defect type from I_D/I_D' is only valid in stage 1, and D' is weak (about 6–7 times the noise at best, much lower for dose 1). Treat vacancy vs sp3 as tentative.

Dose 4 band parameters depend on the baseline model. The rl_series fit and my 2-peak fit differ (D FWHM 41 vs 61 cm^-1; G+D' FWHM 36 vs 47 cm^-1). The D' contribution to G cannot be separated, so G FWHM and position are not clean. The upshift of G to 1592 cm^-1 is mostly D' merging and not doping.
The rl_series band tracker mislabels some bands (D' seen only in dose 3; 2D listed as absent in dose 4). I used my own D/G/D' window fit for ratios; the tracker's heights are fit-model dependent.

The G–2D strain/doping decomposition is only validated at 514 nm. 2D disperses with laser energy, so the 2D position of about 2690 cm^-1 should not be compared with 514 nm values. No strain or doping value is reported.

Whether the dose steps are linear (or what they physically are: ion fluence, plasma time, e-beam, etc.) is unknown, so a defect density versus dose law cannot be fitted. The dose 1 → 3 ratios (1 : 2.3 : 4.8) are only consistent with a roughly proportional growth.

One spectrum per dose on one flake and probably one spot: spot-to-spot variation and focus changes (2D height varies by ±20 %) are not captured. Laser heating at about 1 mW is small for supported 1L (G coefficient about -0.016 cm^-1/K), but a damaged, absorbing dose 4 film could heat more; this is not tested here.

Dose 4 stage 2 reading could also include structural change other than point defects (amorphisation, hydrogenation, oxidation, or PMMA/resist residue with fluorescence background). Spectral data alone cannot separate these.
questions_for_user: What is the treatment (Ar+ sputtering, O2 plasma, e-beam, irradiation, hydrogenation) and what are the actual dose values? Needed to identify defect type and to test whether n_D scales linearly with dose.
Were all four spectra taken at the same spot on the flake, and are there several spots per dose? This separates real dose dependence from spatial variation or edge contribution to D.
What is the SiO2 thickness and was the sample annealed or in air between steps? Needed to interpret the intensity ratios (2D/G ≈ 3, below the ≈ 4 of clean 1L) and any doping change.

Is a second laser wavelength (e.g. 633 or 785 nm) available, or polarisation-resolved spectra? D and 2D disperse while G and hBN-type features do not, and polarisation can reveal edges versus point defects.
Are 1000–1800 cm^-1 spectra with an extended range (e.g. 1700–1800 cm^-1, D+D' near 2950 cm^-1) available for dose 4, together with a background check for fluorescence?

What is the spectral resolution and was the calibration done on the Si line before each spectrum? The Si line at +0.2 cm^-1 offset is consistent, but I assumed the same grating and settings for all four.

What is the SiO2 thickness and was the sample annealed or in air between steps? Needed to interpret the intensity ratios (2D/G ≈ 3, below the ≈ 4 of clean 1L) and any doping change.

Is a second laser wavelength (e.g. 633 or 785 nm) available, or polarisation-resolved spectra? D and 2D disperse while G and hBN-type features do not, and polarisation can reveal edges versus point defects.
Are 1000–1800 cm^-1 spectra with an extended range (e.g. 1700–1800 cm^-1, D+D' near 2950 cm^-1) available for dose 4, together with a background check for fluorescence?

What is the spectral resolution and was the calibration done on the Si line before each spectrum? The Si line at +0.2 cm^-1 offset is consistent, but I assumed the same grating and settings for all four.

structured_output.summary: The defect density rises monotonically with dose. Doses 1–3 are in the low-defect "stage 1" regime, where the D/G height ratio rises 0.25 → 0.57 → 1.19. With the Cancado 2011 relation at 532 nm this gives an inter-defect distance L_D of about 24 → 16 → 11 nm, i.e. n_D of about 5.6e10 → 1.3e11 → 2.7e11 cm^-2 (±~14 % from the relation's constant, plus the ratio uncertainty). Dose 3 is already at the edge of the relation's validity (L_D ≥ 10 nm). Dose 4 has crossed into stage 2. D and G are both strongly broadened (D about 41–61 cm^-1, G+D' about 36–47 cm^-1, depending on the baseline model), D' is merged into G, and the 2D band is nearly gone (<2 % of its dose 1 height). I_D/I_G has dropped back to 0.57, so the L_D relation does not apply. I estimate L_D ≲ 3 nm (n_D ≳ 3.5e12 cm^-2) from the stage boundary only. Given I_D/I_D' ≈ 6–7 in stage 1, the damage looks vacancy-like, but that rests on a weak D' band.

observations.finding: The D band grows strongly and steadily over doses 1–3 while G stays about constant, so the I(D)/I(G) ratio rises. G stays narrow (about 14 cm^-1), which places these spectra in stage 1 (point-defect regime).
observations.evidence: Three-Lorentzian fit of D, G and D' on a linear baseline, 1200–1750 cm^-1. D height 700 → 2047 → 2970 counts; G height 2808 → 3597 → 2494. I_D/I_G (heights) 0.249 → 0.569 → 1.191; by areas 0.26 → 0.60 → 1.26. D position 1345.9 → 1347.3 → 1346.8 cm^-1, FWHM 14.5 / 14.7 / 14.6 cm^-1. G position 1580.3 / 1580.6 / 1580.4 cm^-1, FWHM 13.9 / 14.0 / 13.8 cm^-1. The rl_series fit agrees (D height/G height 0.092/0.366 etc. after its own baseline; D FWHM about 14, G about 12–13). Si offset +0.18 to +0.21 cm^-1 in all spectra, so there is no calibration drift.

observations.finding: The point-defect relation gives L_D and n_D for doses 1–3. Roughly 2× more defects at dose 2 and roughly 5× more at dose 3, relative to dose 1.
observations.evidence: apply_relation graphene_defect_distance_from_ID_IG, laser 532 nm, using height ratios. Dose 1: L_D 24.1 ± 3.3 nm, n_D 5.6e10 cm^-2. Dose 2: 15.9 ± 2.2 nm, 1.28e11 cm^-2. Dose 3: 11.0 ± 1.5 nm, 2.68e11 cm^-2. The errors cover only the ±0.5 in the 1.8e-9 constant, not the fit error on the ratio. n_D is roughly proportional to I_D/I_G in this regime.
observations.source: Cancado et al. 2011, Nano Lett. 11, 3190, Eqs. 3–6 (arXiv 1105.0175)

observations.finding: Dose 4 is in stage 2 (high-defect branch). The D and G bands are strongly broadened, D' is no longer resolved from G, and the 2D band has almost vanished. The L_D relation is therefore not valid, and L_D is only bounded.
observations.evidence: Two-peak fit gives D at 1352.2 cm^-1 with FWHM 61 cm^-1 (the rl_series fit, with a different baseline, gives 1351.9 cm^-1 and 41 cm^-1). The G+D' feature is at 1591.9 cm^-1 with FWHM 47 cm^-1 (rl_series: 1591.8 cm^-1, 36 cm^-1). G+D' is about 3× wider than the stage 1 G (about 14 cm^-1), and its position is raised by the D' merger. I_D/I_G = 0.57 by height and 0.74 by area, lower than dose 3 even though the damage is larger. The 2D region shows only a broad bump of about 100–250 counts, versus 6600–9600 counts in doses 1–3. The wide, merged bands make a precise L_D uncertain. Reading L_D ≲ 3 nm from the stage 1/2 boundary gives n_D ≳ 3.5e12 cm^-2.

observations.finding: D/D' height ratio in stage 1 is about 6–7, closer to vacancy-type defects than to sp3 (about 13) or boundaries (about 3.5). This is a weak, preliminary indication.
observations.evidence: I_D/I_D' = 6.0 (dose 1), 6.2 (dose 2), 6.9 (dose 3), with D' at about 1620–1621 cm^-1 and FWHM 11–13 cm^-1. The D' height is only 116 / 331 / 432 counts against noise of about 60 counts, and the uncertainty on dose 1 is large (D' FWHM ± 4 cm^-1).

caveats: The I_D/I_G ratio is non-monotonic in defect density: it peaks near L_D of about 3 nm and then falls. A single ratio therefore maps to two L_D values. The G FWHM and the 2D band tell the two branches apart. Dose 4 has a lower I_D/I_G than dose 3 but is the most damaged, so ratio alone would mislead.

The Cancado constant was calibrated with Ar+ ion bombardment at 514.5, 632.8 and 785 nm. The tool allows 400–786 nm, so 532 nm is inside its validity range, but this is an interpolation. The lambda^4 scaling and the ±0.5 on 1.8e-9 give about ±14 % on L_D. Absolute numbers carry a larger systematic error than the quoted ±.
Dose 3 (L_D = 11 nm) sits at the lower validity limit (≥ 10 nm) and its I_D/I_G is above 1. The relation probably begins to deviate from linear there, so n_D at dose 3 may be somewhat off.

The relation assumes point defects and low doping. Doping lowers D and D' at a fixed defect count, so ignoring E_F about 0.5 eV could underestimate n_D by more than 2×. Edge or boundary contributions to D (the laser spot may include an edge) would be mistaken for point defects. A single spot per dose cannot separate these.
Defect type from I_D/I_D' is only valid in stage 1, and D' is weak (about 6–7 times the noise at best, much lower for dose 1). Treat vacancy vs sp3 as tentative.

Dose 4 band parameters depend on the baseline model. The rl_series fit and my 2-peak fit differ (D FWHM 41 vs 61 cm^-1; G+D' FWHM 36 vs 47 cm^-1). The D' contribution to G cannot be separated, so G FWHM and position are not clean. The upshift of G to 1592 cm^-1 is mostly D' merging and not doping.
The rl_series band tracker mislabels some bands (D' seen only in dose 3; 2D listed as absent in dose 4). I used my own D/G/D' window fit for ratios; the tracker's heights are fit-model dependent.

The G–2D strain/doping decomposition is only validated at 514 nm. 2D disperses with laser energy, so the 2D position of about 2690 cm^-1 should not be compared with 514 nm values. No strain or doping value is reported.

Whether the dose steps are linear (or what they physically are: ion fluence, plasma time, e-beam, etc.) is unknown, so a defect density versus dose law cannot be fitted. The dose 1 → 3 ratios (1 : 2.3 : 4.8) are only consistent with a roughly proportional growth.

One spectrum per dose on one flake and probably one spot: spot-to-spot variation and focus changes (2D height varies by ±20 %) are not captured. Laser heating at about 1 mW is small for supported 1L (G coefficient about -0.016 cm^-1/K), but a damaged, absorbing dose 4 film could heat more; this is not tested here.

Dose 4 stage 2 reading could also include structural change other than point defects (amorphisation, hydrogenation, oxidation, or PMMA/resist residue with fluorescence background). Spectral data alone cannot separate these.

limits: Dose 4 cannot be quantified: L_D ≲ 3 nm and n_D ≳ 3.5e12 cm^-2 are bounds from the stage 2 criterion, not measurements. The Cancado relation is invalid on the high-defect branch.
The data cannot tell the defect type unambiguously (vacancy vs sp3 vs mixed); the D/D' ratio is weak evidence and only valid in stage 1.
The data cannot separate point defects from edge or grain-boundary D without a spatial map or polarisation series.
The data cannot give a dose–defect law, because the dose values are not known and only one spectrum per step exists.
Doping and strain cannot be extracted: the G–2D vector relation is limited to 514 nm and hole doping, and the measurement is at 532 nm.
Low-frequency modes (< 450 cm^-1) are outside the data window, so shear and layer-breathing modes cannot confirm layer number (the 1L assignment rests on 2D shape and the user's statement).
Laser heating, calibration drift and spot-to-spot differences were checked only indirectly (Si line offset constant at +0.18 to +0.21 cm^-1; power 1 mW for all spectra).
